howTo: Enter the applied tensile or compressive force F in newtons (N).
Enter the resisting cross-sectional area A in square millimetres (mm²).
Select the material grade to establish the reference yield strength Re (MPa).
Review the resulting nominal stress σ = F / A and static safety factor n = Re / σ.
formula: σ = F / A | n = Re / σ

examples.title: Tensile tie rod in structural steel S355
examples.description: A 50 mm solid circular rod (A = 1 963.5 mm²) under a 200 kN axial tensile load.
notes: Stress is well within the elastic capacity of S355 steel with static safety factor n ≈ 3.48.

examples.title: Net plate section under tension
examples.description: A plate with net area A = 300 mm² under a 50 kN axial force using S235 steel.
notes: Safety factor 1.41 indicates marginal capacity under static loading; fatigue or notch sensitivity requires further investigation.

commonMistakes: Entering force in kilonewtons (kN) without converting to newtons (N), leading to an error factor of 1 000 in calculated stress.
Using gross area instead of net area when holes, slots, or cutouts reduce the effective cross-section.
Applying nominal stress directly without checking stress concentration factors (Kt) near geometric discontinuities.
assumptions: Axial load is applied along the centroidal axis with zero eccentricity.
Stress is uniformly distributed across the cross-section (Saint-Venant's principle).
Material is homogeneous, isotropic, and operates strictly within the linear elastic range.
